seoTitle: Get TradingView Premium Free: Legit Trials & Offers
metaDescription: Discover the official ways to access TradingView Premium for free in 2026, from trials to promotions, and how to avoid fake premium unlock scams.
intro: TradingView Premium unlocks extra charts per tab, more indicators, deeper historical data, and a much bigger allowance of price and technical alerts, but there's no permanent free way to keep it. What does exist is an official trial you can run without paying up front, and a plan lineup worth comparing carefully before you pick one. This guide walks the actual pricing and sign-up screens so you know exactly what each tier unlocks, how to start the trial the legitimate way, and why the third-party "free premium unlock" tools floating around are worth ignoring entirely.

steps.heading: Know there's no permanent free Premium tier
steps.body: TradingView's free plan is genuinely usable, but Premium-level features are gated behind a paid subscription — there's no setting or workaround that unlocks it permanently at no cost. Every legitimate route to trying Premium without paying is time-limited: an official trial, a seasonal discount, or a referral credit. Anything claiming to hand you a permanent free unlock outside those channels isn't a real option, it's a scam wearing a tutorial's clothing.

steps.heading: Compare the plan tiers side by side
steps.body: TradingView's pricing page lists four tiers — Essential, Plus, Premium, and Ultimate — each priced per month when billed annually, with the annual option saving noticeably more than paying monthly. Premium sits as the third tier, and its card is highlighted with a distinct border on the pricing page, marking it as the plan most people land on. Every tier below Ultimate also carries a "Try free" button right under the price, which is the legitimate starting point rather than anything you'd find through a browser extension or a third-party generator.

image.caption: The four TradingView plan cards — Essential, Plus, Premium, Ultimate — each showing its monthly price and a built-in free trial button.

steps.heading: Check what each tier actually unlocks
steps.body: Scrolling the feature list under each plan shows exactly what you're paying for as you move up: chart count per tab doubles at each step, indicators per chart go from 5 on the entry tier up into the dozens, and historical bar depth, parallel chart connections, price alerts, and technical alerts all scale up together. Watchlist alerts are a good example of a feature that's completely absent on the lower tiers and only appears once you cross into Premium territory, which is worth checking against your own workflow before assuming you need the top plan.

image.caption: The detailed feature comparison list beneath the plan cards, showing exactly which alert counts and chart limits change at each tier.

steps.heading: Create your account to start the trial
steps.body: Starting the trial routes you through TradingView's own sign-up form — an email address and a password of at least 12 characters with letters and numbers, plus a standard bot check before the account is created. This happens entirely on TradingView's own site, which is the detail that separates a legitimate trial from the fake "free premium" tools that ask you to install something or hand over your existing login instead of creating a fresh account through the official form.

image.caption: TradingView's own sign-up form for starting the trial, asking only for an email and a password — no third-party app or extension involved.

steps.heading: Know what happens when the trial ends
steps.body: Free trials on paid tiers typically require a payment method up front and convert automatically into a paid subscription once the trial window closes, so mark the end date somewhere you'll actually see it. If you decide Premium isn't worth it for your trading style, cancel from your account settings before that date rather than after — once the charge goes through, getting it reversed is a separate hassle from simply not starting it in the first place.

steps.heading: Use referral and seasonal discounts instead of chasing free unlocks
steps.body: Outside of the trial, the legitimate way to lower Premium's cost is TradingView's own referral program and the seasonal promotions it runs directly through its site and app — both reduce what you pay rather than promising to eliminate it. These show up as banners or account credits inside TradingView itself, not as a link from a random video description or a Discord server offering to "activate" your account for a fee.

steps.heading: Avoid fake premium unlock tools
steps.body: Any tool, extension, or generator claiming to unlock Premium for free without going through TradingView's own trial or payment flow is not legitimate, and using one risks your account credentials or payment details being harvested rather than saved. If an offer asks you to log in somewhere other than tradingview.com, download a modified app, or enter card details on a page that isn't clearly TradingView's own checkout, stop and back out — the real trial never requires any of that.

faq.question: Does TradingView offer a permanent free Premium tier?
faq.answer: No, Premium is a paid tier, and any free access comes through official time-limited trials or promotions rather than a permanent free option.

faq.question: Are referral programs a legitimate way to get discounts?
faq.answer: Yes, if TradingView offers an official referral program, using it as intended through your own account is a legitimate way to earn discounts or credits.

faq.question: How can I tell if a 'free premium' offer is a scam?
faq.answer: Be suspicious of any offer outside TradingView's own website or app, especially ones asking you to log in elsewhere, install a modified app, or hand over account credentials or payment details.

faq.question: What happens if I don't cancel before the trial ends?
faq.answer: You'll likely be charged automatically for the plan you trialed once the period ends, since most trials require a payment method up front, so cancel beforehand if you don't want to continue.

faq.question: Which plan should I trial if I'm not sure I need Premium?
faq.answer: Compare the feature list against your actual workflow first — things like watchlist alerts only appear at higher tiers, so check whether you'd use a feature before trialing the plan that includes it.
